description.summary: the compositor's model of apps, windows and Spaces

protocol.description:
The model the desktop shell draws the dock, the app switcher, the bar's menus and Mission Control from: every app with its identity and life, every window with its role, state, place and geometry, and every Space. Windows pair with ext-foreign-toplevel-list handles and Spaces with ext-workspace workspaces; this protocol adds what those do not carry, and the management requests.
State arrives as a burst of events on an object closed by that object's `done`; a client applies the burst atomically. The manager's `done` closes a burst that created or removed objects.
State events that a person or an agent can cause carry the actor that caused them, so the shell can say who moved a window.
Advertised on Shell and Agent connections only. On an Agent connection every request that changes something raises the manager's `not_permitted`.
This protocol is a draft. Until it is declared stable, version 1 may change in place with every client and the server updated together.

interface.name: quire_desktop_manager_v1
interface.description:
On bind the compositor sends an `app`, `window` and `space` event for each existing object, each followed by its state burst, then `active` and `done`.
Version 2 adds `quire_desktop_app_v1.subject`. The objects the manager announces are created at the manager's version, so a client that wants `subject` binds the manager at version 2; a version 1 client sees exactly what it saw before.

request.name: get_window_for

description.summary: the desktop window of a toplevel handle

request.description: Creates a quire_desktop_window_v1 for the window an ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 names. Its state burst follows at once.

request.name: create_space

description.summary: add a Space on an output

request.description: The new Space arrives as a `space` event.

request.name: stop
request.description: The compositor sends no more `app`, `window` or `space` events and answers with `finished`.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Valid after `finished`. Objects already created stay valid.

event.name: app
event.description: Its state burst follows on the new object.

event.name: window
event.description: Its state burst follows on the new object.

event.name: space
event.description: Its state burst follows on the new object.

event.name: active

description.summary: the active app and key window changed

event.description: Null when no app is active, or when the active app has no key window.

event.name: finished

description.summary: no more events on the manager

event.description: Sent after `stop`, or when the compositor withdraws the global. The client destroys the manager.

interface.name: quire_desktop_app_v1
interface.description: An app is the set of windows and processes with one app key. Its state burst ends with `done`; `closed` ends its life (the client destroys the object).

description.summary: how the compositor knows who the app is

entry.name: scope
entry.summary: the app's systemd scope, made by our launcher

entry.name: claimed
entry.summary: only what the app says (xdg_toplevel app id)

description.summary: where the app is in its life
whether the app's windows are hidden
where the app's global menu comes from
how much the app asks for the person

event.name: identity
event.description: `key` is the app key the rest of the desktop names the app by. `claimed_id` is what the app says about itself, which may differ from `key` when `proof` is not `claimed`.

arg.name: claimed_id
arg.summary: the app id the app claims

description.summary: the app was hidden or shown

event.name: menu_source

description.summary: where to read the app's global menu

event.description: `bus` is the D-Bus name; `app_path` and `menubar_path` are object paths, empty when the source has none.

description.summary: the app's request for attention changed

event.name: mru

description.summary: the app's place in recent use

event.description: 0 is the most recently active app.

event.name: closed
event.description: The last event of the app's life; the client destroys the object.

event.name: subject

description.summary: the program behind the app, as the compositor established it

event.description:
The program image path (an absolute path) for a native process, or the sandbox's app id for a sandboxed one. It is a fact the compositor established about the process that owns the app's windows (it holds the process, reads the image the system owns, or has the sandbox vouch for the app), not a claim the app made: unlike `claimed_id` it can be compared with the standing of another process, such as the owner of the app's menu on the session bus.
Sent in the app's state burst, after `identity`, and again if the program behind the app changes. Never sent for a program the compositor cannot name (an image the person can write, a process that has gone, a program that changed its image after it connected): no event means no subject is known, not that the subject is empty.

arg.name: subject
arg.summary: an image path or a sandbox app id

request.name: activate
request.description: Activates the app and raises its windows. `serial` is the serial of the input event that led to the request.

request.name: quit
request.description: The app may refuse or ask the person first.

request.name: reopen

description.summary: activate an app with no windows

request.description: The compositor answers with quire_shell_v1.reopen to the shell.

interface.name: quire_desktop_window_v1
interface.description: A toplevel the compositor manages. Its state burst ends with `done`; `closed` is its last event.

entry.name: window_modal
entry.summary: a sheet: blocks its parent window

description.summary: whether an agent holds the window
which Spaces the window is assigned to

entry.name: none
entry.summary: no assignment: it stays where it opens

event.name: identifier
event.description: The identifier the window's ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 carries. Sent once.

description.summary: the app the window belongs to

event.name: place
event.description: `space` is the Space for `on_space` and null for `all_spaces`.

description.summary: the output the window is mostly on

event.name: geometry
event.description: In global logical pixels, and the scale of its output in 120ths.

event.name: parent
event.description: Null for a window without a parent.

event.name: sensitivity
event.description: The strongest level any of the window's surfaces declares.

event.name: lease

description.summary: an agent's hold on the window

event.description: `glow` is the run's glow; `off` when the state is `free`.

event.name: menu_path

description.summary: the window's own menu object path

event.description: The object path of this window's menu under its app's menu source; empty when the window uses the app's menu.

event.name: closed
event.description: The last event; the client destroys the object.

request.name: activate
request.description: `serial` is the serial of the input event that led to the request.

description.summary: minimise the window into the dock
bring the window back from the dock
move the window to a Space

interface.name: quire_desktop_space_v1
interface.description: A Space is a desktop of one output, or a full-screen or Split View window's own Space, or an agent's task Space. Its state burst ends with `done`; `removed` is its last event.

description.summary: what is happening on the Space

entry.name: agent_running
entry.summary: an agent run is working there

event.name: id
event.description: The stable Space id the rest of the desktop keys on; also the ext-workspace `id`. Sent once.

event.name: occupant

description.summary: the task the Space belongs to

event.description: An opaque task token for an `agent` Space; empty otherwise.

event.name: position

description.summary: the Space's position on its output

event.description: 0 is the leftmost.

description.summary: what is happening on the Space

event.name: removed
event.description: The last event; the client destroys the object.

request.name: remove
request.description: Its windows move to the neighbouring desktop Space.

description.summary: move the Space on its output
